body.estimand_functional: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}I_{j,n}(\alpha))\), with the optimal weak-separation benchmark \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)\)

sampling_model.design: Fixed finite treated groups and prespecified donor stacks. Each donor stack has known comparison-group weights, and its score is exactly the treated-minus-donor contrast in the baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case-mix summaries collected in \(G_{ri}\).
sampling_model.units: At each \(n\), the observable sample has the product joint law \(\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\); the model is the full triangular array \(\mathbf P=(\mathbb P_n)_{n\ge1}\).
sampling_model.treatment: A fixed realized group-level treatment history. Consistency and the shared-slope additive untreated-change model give the causal interpretation, conditional on the score containing every systematic untreated-trend predictor.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive group has a limiting sample fraction bounded away from zero; no treatment-propensity overlap condition is used.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Group means and within-group covariance matrices are estimated directly; the known contrast matrix propagates shared treated and reused-control covariance. The symmetric covariance estimator is spectrally clipped to \([\underline\omega/2,2\overline\omega]\), so all feasible inverses and critical values are defined. The diagnostic report records score uncertainty, any documented ex ante population-total calibration, held-out placebo trends, omitted-predictor balance, donor leverage, and effective sample sizes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Projection intervals are universally valid after noisy winner selection but can be substantially longer than selection-tailored intervals.
Bayes--minimax duality characterizes confidence sets minimizing worst-case expected measure for restricted Gaussian location parameters.
Simultaneous inference yields universal validity after arbitrary model selection at a possible precision cost.
Subsequence arguments give GMM inference uniform over unidentified, weak, semi-strong, and strong regimes.
Conditional Gaussian inference controls size uniformly without imposing identification-strength restrictions.
Few-treated-group difference-in-differences inference accommodates heteroskedasticity induced by unequal group sizes using many controls.
Cross-fitted bias correction and self-normalization yield average synthetic-control-effect inference under time-series asymptotics.
Theorem 1.1 establishes global Le Cam equivalence between i.i.d. density estimation and Gaussian white noise over densities in a Hölder ball with exponent above one half and bounded away from zero.

body.tldr: A small fixed menu of prespecified donor stacks creates a nonregular inference problem when validity is exact equality of a noisy score containing baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case mix. Under an almost-sure shared-slope model for untreated post-minus-pre changes, iterated expectations make exact score equality imply the same ATT for every close donor. Spectral clipping totalizes the feasible joint Gaussian profiles, which are uniformly honest on this conditional triangular-array class and root-sample narrow under fixed separation. An explicitly two-dimensional donor-switch experiment has an exact likelihood-ratio minimax rule, reducing worst-case expected diameter from \(0.3475\) for a defined Gaussian maximum benchmark to \(0.2165\). The general finite-face frontier and transfer from a restricted QMD reduced-mean experiment remain open. Ranked near-balance does not validate the historical CMS estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel methods use many untreated groups, synthetic-control methods use long time series, and generic post-selection methods do not optimize confidence-set diameter for a target whose label is defined by an exact zero score.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused groups, and uncertainty about which comparisons satisfy a prespecified exact transport score. Its causal interpretation requires both an exact population equality and a transparent model connecting the score to untreated changes; ranked sample balance supplies neither.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact-close transport by iterated expectations under an almost-sure shared-slope untreated-change model, supplies falsifying calibration and placebo diagnostics, proves conditional uniform validity and fixed-separation oracle behavior for a spectrally clipped joint inversion, solves the embedded two-donor honest-diameter problem exactly, and leaves general face-adaptive minimaxity and restricted QMD reduced-experiment transfer as explicit open questions.

body.related_work: RTI International documents a CMS comparison-state workflow based on ranked baseline distance, two or three retained states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting. The reviewed methods source does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known administrative population totals. Observed ranked near-balance therefore does not prove exact equality, and the exact-face theorem does not validate the historical CMS estimates; the workflow is only a motivating, falsifiable use case. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto treat few policy-changing groups, but their reference distribution comes from many controls rather than many micro observations inside fixed labels. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu's JPE article, \emph{Debiasing and t-Tests for Synthetic Control Inference on Average Causal Effects}, develops cross-fitted debiasing and self-normalized t-tests for synthetic-control average causal effects, not exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. justify universal post-selection coverage through simultaneity. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey show why projection is honest but potentially imprecise after noisy option selection. Evans, Hansen, and Stark provide the acceptance-region Bayes--minimax template that informs the stratified target-map problem. Andrews and Cheng and Andrews and Mikusheva supply weak-identification asymptotics but not deficiency or expected-diameter risk transfer on donor faces. Nussbaum's Theorem 1.1 and Section 2 establish full deficiency equivalence through domination, Hölder smoothness above one half, positivity, compact parameter control, and explicit likelihood-process approximation; these stronger ingredients explain why fourth moments alone cannot support an unrestricted raw-data equivalence claim here. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato justify covariance-estimated Gaussian maxima, which support the feasible benchmark rather than its decision-theoretic optimality.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The explicit Gaussian maximum benchmark fails the early optimality test. In the two-donor identity-covariance switch with \(c=1\), \(\Delta=0.4\), and \(\alpha=0.05\), its worst expected diameter is \(0.3475\), while the exact Neyman--Pearson value is \(0.2165\); the elementary total-variation bound \(0.1518\) is not sharp. General optimized inversion remains open, and transfer beyond a restricted QMD or reduced-sample-mean experiment is not claimed.
body.honest_scope: Uniform coverage and fixed-separation root-sample diameter are theorem targets only over the exact-close triangular-array class satisfying the almost-sure shared-slope additive untreated-change model, with every feasible inverse and critical value computed from the spectrally clipped covariance matrix. Diagnostics can reveal failures of calibration, placebo fit, omitted-predictor balance, or donor support, but ranked empirical near-balance does not prove exact population equality or causal transport. No reviewed source documents ex ante CMS algebraic calibration to known administrative population totals, so the exact-face results do not validate the historical CMS estimates. The exact embedded two-donor minimax formula and the explicit Gaussian maximum benchmark are theorem targets. General multiple-face minimax optimality and transfer from a restricted QMD reduced experiment under separate uniform-integrability conditions are open-ended questions; unrestricted raw-data Le Cam equivalence and maximum-critical optimality are not claimed.
